- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml line 672 with scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 22033
  Line or code reference: The `if: steps.find_tracking.outputs.has_work == 'true'` gate on the `Process each tracking issue` step at workflow line 672, which is the only step that runs `bash scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, prevents `release_staged_support_needs_human_latches` at script line 22033 from executing on any tick where no open `ai:orchestrator-tracking` issues exist.
  Problem: A staged-support `ai:needs-human` latch on an issue whose tracking project has completed and whose tracking issue is closed is never swept. The sweep is also skipped during quiet periods when no project is active, even though a latch from a prior project still needs release. The function is correctly called at line 22033 but the entire job step never runs when `has_work` is `false`.
  Why it fails at runtime: The `#4113` scenario this PR fixes — a staged-support latch outliving its project — is exactly the case where the tracking issue may already be closed or no tracking issues remain. The sweep designed to release those latches never starts.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: line 14607 — `issue_labels_json="$(... jq -c ... 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"`
  Problem: When jq fails to extract labels from a latched issue's JSON (pipe error, memory exhaustion, corrupted data), the fallback `[]` is treated as an empty label set.
  Why it fails at runtime: The guard at line 14608 that checks for `ai:destructive-blocked` and `ai:scope-blocked` receives `[]` and proceeds to release the latch as if no safety latches are present. An issue carrying these human-gated labels would have `ai:needs-human` removed without the operator's involvement.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 14681-14691 — compensation branch when `/approved` comment POST fails and the compensating label-edit to restore `ai:needs-human` also fails
  Problem: After the label swap at lines 14672-14675 succeeds (issue is now `ai:awaiting-approval` without `ai:needs-human`), the comment POST for `/approved` fails (line 14681). The code attempts to restore `ai:needs-human` via a compensating label edit (lines 14683-14684). If that edit also fails, the issue remains in `ai:awaiting-approval` with no `ai:needs-human` and only warning logs.
  Why it fails at runtime: Stall recovery at `run_standalone_stall_recovery` maps `ai:awaiting-approval` to `auto_approve`, which re-posts `/approved`. A transient double API failure can convert a human-gated issue into autonomously resumed implementation with no durable record of the latch.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: line 22033 (call site) and .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:672 (the `if: steps.find_tracking.outputs.has_work == 'true'` gate on the enclosing `Process each tracking issue` step)
  Problem: `release_staged_support_needs_human_latches` is invoked at line 22033, inside the poller step that .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml gates with `if: steps.find_tracking.outputs.has_work == 'true'`. `has_work` is set to `true` only when at least one open `ai:orchestrator-tracking` issue exists (orchestrate_poll.yml:212-220). A source-repository tick where every orchestrator project has completed and the tracking issue is closed (or where no project ever existed) silently skips the entire poller step, so any `ai:needs-human` latch set by `scripts/implement_handle_guard_block.sh` is never visited.
  Why it fails at runtime: an implement run that hits `IMPLEMENT_STAGED_SUPPORT_REBASE_CONFLICT` after its project has been completed/closed (or a standalone implement on `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows` with no orchestrator tracking issue present, e.g. an unrelated bot-driven code fix) parks `ai:needs-human` indefinitely. The "stale `no_labels` on closed issues" reconciliation that handles other terminal states does not apply here because the issue stays open with `ai:needs-human`; the only recovery path in current code is a human comment, exactly the dead-end the PR is meant to close.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 14672-14691
  Problem: the latch-release compensation is not fail-closed. When the `/approved` comment POST (line 14681) fails after the `gh issue edit` succeeded (line 14672-14673 swapped the labels to `ai:awaiting-approval`), the script calls a second `gh issue edit` (line 14683) to restore `ai:needs-human`. If that compensation `gh issue edit` also fails, the script only emits `STAGED_SUPPORT_LATCH_SKIP issue=N reason=approval_comment_failed_compensation_failed` and `continue`s, leaving the issue carrying `ai:awaiting-approval` without `ai:needs-human`.
  Why it fails at runtime: `STALL_RECOVERY_ACTIONS` in `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py` maps `ai:awaiting-approval` to `auto_approve` (executed by `execute_stall_recovery_action` and `run_standalone_stall_recovery`). Both orchestrator-managed and standalone stall recovery treat the issue as waiting on human approval and can re-dispatch `implement.yml`. Without `ai:needs-human` to gate the run, a transient double GitHub-API failure silently converts a staged-support latch into autonomous resume; the warning log is the only signal, and it is not consulted by stall recovery. `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` covers the single-failure path (`reason=approval_comment_failed_latch_restored`) but does not exercise the double-failure path this concern identifies.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: line 14607
  Problem: per-issue label extraction falls back to the literal string `[]` on any `jq` failure: `issue_labels_json="$(... | jq -c '...' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"`. The downstream safety check on line 14608 (`index("ai:destructive-blocked") != null or index("ai:scope-blocked") != null`) reads an empty label list and silently passes, so the `STAGED_SUPPORT_LATCH_SKIP reason=other_human_gated_latch_present` path is never taken when label parsing fails.
  Why it fails at runtime: `ai:destructive-blocked` and `ai:scope-blocked` are human safety latches documented elsewhere in the same script; their purpose is exactly to stop autonomous poller action. The fallback turns a parse failure into "no safety latches present" and lets the sweep remove `ai:needs-human` from an issue that genuinely carries one of those labels. The fix is a small fail-closed change (treat jq failure as `STAGED_SUPPORT_LATCH_SKIP reason=labels_unavailable` and continue), but the current fallback is a defense-in-depth gap on a human-safety guard.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

The safety check fails open on the exact data it exists to verify.

- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 212-216 (`has_work=false` when zero open `ai:orchestrator-tracking` issues) gating the `Process each tracking issue` step at line 672 (`if: steps.find_tracking.outputs.has_work == 'true'`), which is the step that runs `bash scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`; the new sweep is invoked only from inside that script at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:22033
  Problem: `release_staged_support_needs_human_latches` never executes on any poll tick with no open orchestrator tracking issue, because the entire poller step is skipped.
  Why it fails at runtime: implement.yml's staged-support rejection handler is not orchestrator-only — any approved issue (including standalone, non-orchestrator issues) can be latched `ai:needs-human` by `IMPLEMENT_STAGED_SUPPORT_REBASE_CONFLICT`, and an orchestrator-managed issue can outlive its project's tracking issue. In the source repository, whenever no project is active, the cron tick exits at "No active orchestrator projects" and the latch is never swept — the feature this PR ships silently does nothing in exactly the quiet periods where a parked issue most needs an unattended release. The sweep (or a thin wrapper invoking just it) needs to run from a step that is not gated on `has_work`.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
